title: Senior's toolkit: investigation and rescue
summary: bisect run, pickaxe search, log -L, blame that sees through moves, worktrees, filter-repo and line endings.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: investigation and rescue
steps.body: When something broke and nobody knows when or why, these commands answer "which commit", "who changed this and why", and "how do I fix it without stopping my other work".

toolkit.what: Binary-searches history for the commit that broke something, running your test at each step. 1000 commits take about 10 runs.
flags: start with a bad and a known good commit
exit 0 = good, 1-127 = bad, 125 = skip this commit
go back to where you started
toolkit.example:
git bisect start HEAD v2.3.0
git bisect run dotnet test --filter Discount
git bisect reset
toolkit.when: a regression with a reproducible test

toolkit.what: The pickaxe: finds commits that added or removed a string. `-G` matches a regex in any changed line.
flags: commits where the count of that text changed
commits whose diff has a matching line

toolkit.what: The history of one function: every commit that changed it, with only that function's diff.
Who last changed each line, ignoring whitespace changes and following code that was moved or copied from other files.
flags: follow lines moved or copied between files

toolkit.what: A second working folder on another branch from the same repository. Fix a production bug without stashing or losing your build.
flags: create a new branch for it
toolkit.when: an urgent fix interrupts a big change

toolkit.what: Rewrites all history to remove a file, such as a committed secret. Rotate the secret first: the old value is already compromised.
flags: remove the selected paths instead of keeping them
replace strings such as a password everywhere
toolkit.when: a secret or a huge file reached history

toolkit.what: A `.gitattributes` line that stores text files with LF and stops the "every line changed" diffs between Windows and Linux.
flags: let Git detect text files and normalise them
check them out with LF everywhere
override for files that need CRLF
re-apply the rules to files already committed
toolkit.example:
printf '* text=auto eol=lf\n' > .gitattributes
git add --renormalize .
git commit -m "Normalise line endings"

steps.prompt: Match each command to the question it answers.
pairs: when was this string added or removed?
how did this one function change over time?
who wrote these lines, ignoring moves and reformatting?
how do I fix main without touching my current work?

steps.prompt: Since some point in the last 600 commits, orders over 100 euros get the wrong discount. A unit test reproduces it. What is the fastest way to find the commit?
options: `git bisect start HEAD <last good tag>` then `git bisect run` with the test
Check out commits one by one from the newest
steps.explain: Bisect halves the range each time: 600 commits need about 10 test runs, done automatically. `blame` only shows the last change to each line, which may not be the one that caused the bug.

steps.prompt: A teammate on Windows edited one line of `deploy.sh`, and the pull request shows all 200 lines as changed. `git diff --ignore-all-space` shows one line. What is the lasting fix?
options: Add `* text=auto eol=lf` to `.gitattributes` and run `git add --renormalize .`
Ask the teammate to use another editor
Set `core.autocrlf false` on your own machine
steps.explain: The file was committed with CRLF line endings. `.gitattributes` is committed, so the rule applies to everyone regardless of their personal settings, and `--renormalize` fixes the files already in the repository.

steps.prompt: Find the bad commit between now and tag `v2.3.0` automatically.
steps.explain: `start` takes the bad commit first, then a good one. `run` calls the script on each candidate: exit 0 marks it good, 1-127 (except 125) bad, 125 skips it.

steps.prompt: A cloud access key was committed and pushed a week ago. Put the response in order.
lines: Revoke and rotate the key in the cloud console
Ask everyone to re-clone and ask GitHub support to purge cached views
steps.explain: Rotate first: rewriting history does not un-leak a key that bots may already have scraped. `filter-repo` removes the `origin` remote as a safety measure, so you add it back before force-pushing.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: When you are asked "when did this break?", write a failing test and let `bisect run` find it. Before you change old code, run `git log -L` or `blame -w -C -C` on it to read the commit that explains why it is that way. Add a `.gitattributes` to every new repository on day one.
